label: ports-graded-probe
_why: §10.60 VALIDATION PROBE (graded port factorisation, canonical config): port tiers now emit at 1/10 (e0-e2) and 1/5 (e3-e4) unit size - goods+building_cost divided EXPLICITLY in the config (user architecture 2026-08-16: no hidden divisor; UI-visible), employment/state-effects scaled at emission by the per-tier workforce_mult/effect_mult fields (0.1/0.1/0.1/0.2/0.2), and the 1836 start's port levels multiplied by 1/workforce_mult (anchorage-mapped entries clamped at exactly level 1). SUCCESS: the F66 provisioning waves REAPPEAR (engine-side, un-suppressible - that is expected and fine) but at ~1/10 cost (a steam port = 40 anchor pts); GBR's queue share of port_steam collapses from ~47% to single digits; hub ports grow ~x10 levels to carry the same shipping lanes (lane MM demand is engine-side and ABSOLUTE); steamer market + metal-yard adoption readable in the same window; colonial market access stays ~1.0. FAILURE MODES to check: (a) the engine TRUNCATING fractional goods/infra values (port MM output 0 => convoy collapse, port profit weird - read GBR merchant marine + port building profit in the save summaries), (b) hub ports NOT growing (lane capacity starved), (c) construction still port-dominated (queue_mix). Watch NET/SPA/POR/DEN delayed waves when they research screw_frigate (~1848) in queue_mix.
_arms: graded = {kind: config, config: config/mod_config.json} - the CANONICAL config as of 2026-08-16 evening: graded port factorisation (§10.60) + canonical nice_to_have infra subsidies + F61 slave model. Needs build.ps1 >= 2026-08-16 evening (QtyMul fractional emission + workforce_mult/effect_mult) and convert_history.ps1 same (level multiply + anchorage clamp).
_comparison: vancost-nosub-n2 (20260816_011552) is the pre-fix wave shape: GBR queue 100% port_steam 1837-41 -> 12 lv, FRA -> 10 by 1841, port_industrial wave from ~1849, GBR GDP 0.57 of vanilla by ~1855. ports_aival probes (16.08) proved ai_value inert against the provisioning term.
_cost: 1 run x 16 in-game years, ~20 min wall.
